The plaintiff's witnesses failed to establish the condition nos. 3 and 4 of the deed of the agreement dated 11.12.1991 but on the other hand by series of legal notices the case of the defendants is proved. The learned advocate lastly submits that violation of the conditions of Exhibit-`Gha' i.e. the deed of agreement dated 11.12. I991 can be a ground for the plaintiff to get the relief prayed, but it is not proved and in fixing the burden of proof the learned appellate court below is totally misconceived and instead of the plaintiff the learned Additional District Judge, 211(1 Court, Dhaka fixed the burden on the defendant arbitrarily while the trial court rightly fixed the burden of proof on the plaintiff which is not proved at-all. Within the pleading of the plaintiff in his plaint the existence of the deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991 is absent and as such the plaint is vague and unspecified where as the entire case of the plaintiff depends upon violation of the conditions cited within the contents of the deed dated 11.12.1991 marked as Exhibit- `Ga'. Despite the plaintiff failed to prove the violation of conditions of Exhibit-'Ga' the learned lower appellate court decreed the suit in his favour which is perverse and not under the ambit of relevant laws. It is not proved by any evidence that the defendant has failed to repay the amount 1,60,000/- (one lac and sixty thousand) by the stipulated time as mentioned within the condition of the deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991. The learned counsel on behalf of the petitioner submits that the defendant have no subsisting interest in the land of agreement as the defendant with the consent of the plaintiff sold out the property in favour of 3rd party who after his purchase mutated his name and subsequently transferred the suit land in favour of 4th party which is mentioned by the defendants in where pleading within the written statement. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule controverts the argument advanced from the side of the learned advocate for the petitioner and submits that the learned court of appeal below during disposal of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity and rightly held that the trial court during disposal of the original suit committed error of law as well as facts and in deciding the fate of the suit there has been miscourage of justice. Considering the said aspect the appellate court below after proper sifting of evidence and consideration of facts decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the plaintiff-appellant rightly and after the impugned judgment and decree the plaintiff have already obtained the kabala deed registered through court. The learned advocate further submits that by supplementary agreement the onus of proving the respective plea of the defendant has been sifted to her that she tried to give the money back within the stipulated time as mentioned within the content of the deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991 marked as Exhibit-`Ga'. Admittedly the .defendant received a sum of Tk. 1,60,000/-(one lac and sixty thousand) from the plaintiff and it is the incumbent duty upon the defendant to establish her case by cogent, competent credible evidence that she ever tried to return the money back to the plaintiff within the time specified in the content of the document which is a admitted deed of agreement between the parties. The learned advocate for the opposite party also submits that admittedly the original deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991 after its signing was kept within the custody of the defendant which is the backbone of the suit. It is the definite condition within the document that the sum of Tk. 1,60,000/4one lac and sixty thousand) is to be refunded by the defendant in favour of the plaintiff within 21.03.1992 but the defendant has failed to prove that she ever made any effort to refund the amount in favour of the plaintiff. The learned advocate lastly submits that by execution of second agreement the terms -and conditions of the first agreement have become redundant and in consultation with the evidence on record properly the learned appellate court below rightly held that the fact of returning the amount or any effort to repay the amount by the defendant within the stipulated time not at-all proved rather disproved by the defendant's witnesses. The witness no. 2 for the defendant Ismail Khan is totally silent about the second agreement while it is the case of the defendant that through him the defendant tried to repay the amount by 21.03.1992. Apart from this: this witness Ismail Khan did not corroborate the witness no. 01 of the defendant on the specific case that she (defendant) tried to repay the amount in favour of the plaintiff. Besides this, the witness no. 03 for the plaintiff Haji Hanif did not corroborate the defendant's case that the son of the defendant i.e. the witness no. 02 for the defendant ever went before him with money on 21.03.1992. Under Section 103 of the Evidence Act the burden of proof is entirely lies upon the defendant and the lower appellate court rightly observed in his findings that in discharging the onus the defendant has hopelessly failed and that the plaintiff has successfully proved his bonafide. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the opposite party taking notice of the case record argued that no legal notice was given to the plaintiff for taking the money in between 11.12.1991 to 21.03.1992. Lastly; there is no misrepresentation of facts, non-consideration of material evidence and misreading or non-reading of evidence from the side of the learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka during disposal of the appeal by which it can be held that any error of law was done by the lower appellate court in passing the impugned judgment and decree and as such there is nothing to interfere with the same. 

 11. In view of the above facts of the case we have come-across from the documentaly evidence that by supplementary agreement deed dated 11.12.1991 the initial contract between the parties has become redundant. In this context; it is obvious to note that the burden of proof which was initially fixed upon the plaintiff has been obviously sifted upon the defendant by the very inception of the supplementary deed of agreement dated 11.12.1991 marked as exhibit-'Gha' and in this regard; it is the positive case of the defendant-petitioner that she offered the sum of Tk. 1,60,000/-(one lac and sixty thousand) which was admittedly taken by her to the plaintiff by the stipulated time but the plaintiff refused to accept the same. 

 14. Going through the evidence on record it is apparent that the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal fixing the onus of proof upon the defendant no. 01 to show that she offered Tk. 1,60,000/- (one lac and sixty thousand) to the plaintiff on or before 21.03.1992 held that the defendant has failed to discharge the onus that she ever offered the amount in favour of the plaintiff by the stipulated time and in this context; I have every reason to incline such a view that by the execution of second agreement paper the responsibility has been sifted upon the defendant to discharge the onus in proving that she ever tried to repay the amount which was admittedly taken by her from the plaintiff. Under Section 103 of the Evidence Act the lower appellate court was quite justified in holding that the onus of proving the fact that the defendant tried to repay the amount lies upon her. On perusal of the plaint it transpires that, it has been clearly stated therein that the terms of the contract was not complied with by the defendant-petitioner and having failed to get the kabala deed registered after its execution from the defendant the plaintiff filed the original suit for specific performance of contract. 

 16. Upon the pleadings of the parties the evidence adduced go to show that the plaintiff's witnesses by their testimony corroborated the case of the plaintiff as to the existence of the deed of agreement payment of partial consideration amount and non-payment of the amount from the side of the vendor in favour of the vendee which was accepted by her pursuant to the initial deed of agreement. The legal notices marked as Exhibits- '3' and '4' also supports the case of the plaintiff and the witnesses who deposed except some minor discrepancies corroborated the plaint case in tow which is properly assessed and evaluated by the learned court of appeal below during disposal of the appeal. The legal notices which were sent by the plaintiff in favour of the defendants also proves his bonafide and as such the onus of proving the plaintiff's case has been successfully discharged by tangible evidence on record which was considered during deciding the merit of the appeal rightly. Hence, obviously the plaintiff to the suit has done his part as per agreement and was also willing to repay the balance consideration. But in the instant case the part of proof i.e. the burden of proof which was imposed upon the defendant by the very execution of the second deed of agreement dated 11.12.1 991 not proved rather disproved.
